_note: Champagne in depth (pipeline/champagne.py). Zones and terroirs follow the UMC aire géographique tables, which keep Val du Petit Morin, Côte de Sézanne, Vitryat and Montgueux inside a wider Côte des Blancs; here they are zones of their own. Échelle des crus ratings from secondary lists that agree with each other; the AOC specification lists only the names of the grand and premier cru communes. Breuil-sur-Vesle is in the AOC list but not in the UMC tables: zone by proximity, no area.

doubts: Sub-region scheme: zone and terroir assignments come from the UMC tables (4 zones, 17 terroirs, 319 communes, sums match exactly). UMC puts Côte de Sézanne (Sézannais), Vitryat, Montgueux and Val du Petit Morin inside its Côte des Blancs zone. I kept them as separate sub-regions; 'umc_zone' and 'umc_terroir' on each commune allow folding them back. Val du Petit Morin (19 input communes, incl. premier crus Étréchy, Val-des-Marais/Coligny, Villeneuve-Renneville-Chevigny) is a UMC terroir name not on the requested list; fold into Côte des Blancs if you need only the listed names.

Comité Champagne (champagne.fr) uses four main areas without per-commune lists on the pages I could read. INAO lists 14 viticultural regions (e.g. Région de Congy-Villevenard, Vallée du Surmelin) but no commune mapping.
Tours-sur-Marne: UMC places it in the Grande Vallée de la Marne; many guides list it with the Montagne de Reims grands crus. I followed UMC (Vallée de la Marne).
Villenauxe-la-Grande (Aube) is listed by UMC in the Barséquanais (Côte des Bar), though geographically it adjoins the Côte de Sézanne. Followed UMC.

Breuil-Sur-Vesle is not in the UMC 319-commune tables. ABC du Vin lists 'Breuil' in the Marne grape-growing zone (213 Marne communes vs 212 in UMC). Subregion Montagne de Reims (Vesle valley) is my assignment by proximity, not from a source. Vineyard area unknown, probably tiny.

Bligny: two AOC communes share the name, Bligny (Aube, Bar-sur-Aubois, 160.4 ha) and Bligny (Marne, Vesle & Ardre, 5.2 ha). The input has one key; I mapped it to the Aube commune and put the Marne one under 'homonym'. Check which one the EU list meant (it may cover both).

Échelle percentages are not in the official specification (it lists only names). Values come from secondary sources that agree with each other (thefinestbubble, champagneclub, wein.plus, krasiagr). Disagreements: Bergères-lès-Vertus 95 (champagneclub splits 95 white / 90 black); Bezannes and Cormontreuil missing from some lists; champagneclub wrongly shows Épernay at 94 and 95. Coulommes-la-Montagne, Sermiers and Vrigny are 90 since 2003 (were 89), so older lists omit them.

Premier cru count: 42 in the AOC specification section II.c; 44 in sources that add Chouilly (Pinot Noir) and Tours-sur-Marne (Chardonnay); some lists show 41 to 43 because of double entries. The input yields 37 premier cru communes plus 5 premier crus inside merged communes (Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, Bisseuil, Vertus, Voipreux, Tauxières) = 42.

End of the échelle: sources disagree. wine-law.org and BKWine say abandoned from the 2004 harvest (indicative prices stopped 2001); GuildSomm and champagneclub say 2010. The 22 Nov 2010 decree repealed the 1952 decree and kept the grand/premier cru commune lists in the specification.

The current specification still names pre-merger communes (Ay, Mareuil-sur-Ay, Bisseuil, Louvois, Tauxières, Oger, Vertus, Voipreux, Coligny (Val-des-Marais), Villeneuve-Renneville). Whether premier cru/grand cru applies to the whole merged commune or only the former commune territory is assumed to be the latter; not explicitly verified.
Gionges (part of Blancs-Coteaux) appears only in the élaboration zone per ABC du Vin, not the grape-growing zone; not verified in an official source.
Aÿ-Champagne English Wikipedia contradicts itself (grand cru 100% vs premier cru 99%); 99% applies to Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, 100% to Aÿ per the specification and échelle lists.
UMC area figures carry no year. Total vineyard figures range 34,183 to 34,317 ha depending on source and year; I used SGV 2023 data (34,200 ha).
Tauxières percentage 99 is from secondary lists; Wein.plus names it Tauxières-Mutry.

Montagne de Reims.atlas_note: The wooded plateau between Reims and Épernay, with vines on its north, east and south slopes. Pinot Noir leads, above all in the nine grand cru villages of the Grande Montagne. The zone also takes in the Massif de Saint-Thierry, the Monts de Berru and the Vesle and Ardre valleys.
Montagne de Reims.grape_share_note: Share of the planted area of the zone. Union des Maisons de Champagne (UMC), aire géographique tables; the year is not given.
rules: UMC terroir Grande Montagne de Reims

Vallée de la Marne.atlas_note: The largest zone. It follows the Marne from east of Épernay west into the Aisne and the Seine-et-Marne. Meunier leads on the clay slopes of the valley. The Grande Vallée around Aÿ is Pinot Noir country, with the grands crus of Aÿ and Tours-sur-Marne.
Vallée de la Marne.grape_share_note: Share of the planted area of the zone. Union des Maisons de Champagne (UMC), aire géographique tables; the year is not given.

Côte des Blancs.atlas_note: An east-facing chalk slope running south from Épernay to Vertus. It is almost all Chardonnay. Six of the 17 grand cru villages are here.
Côte des Blancs.grape_share_note: Share of the planted area of the zone. Union des Maisons de Champagne (UMC), aire géographique tables; the year is not given.
Côte des Blancs.vine_area_note: The Côte des Blancs proper, 10 communes. With the Val du Petit Morin, Côte de Sézanne, Vitryat and Montgueux, the wider zone of the Union des Maisons de Champagne covers 6,304 ha.

Val du Petit Morin.atlas_note: Twenty communes around the marshes of Saint-Gond, between the Côte des Blancs and the Côte de Sézanne. Chardonnay leads, with much Meunier. The houses' union counts it in a wider Côte des Blancs.
Val du Petit Morin.grape_share_note: Share of the planted area of the zone. Union des Maisons de Champagne (UMC), aire géographique tables; the year is not given.

Côte de Sézanne.atlas_note: Slopes around Sézanne in the south of the Marne. Chardonnay leads. The houses' union counts it in a wider Côte des Blancs.
Côte de Sézanne.grape_share_note: Share of the planted area of the zone. Union des Maisons de Champagne (UMC), aire géographique tables; the year is not given.

Vitryat.atlas_note: A small outlying area around Vitry-le-François in the east of the Marne. It is almost all Chardonnay. The houses' union counts it in a wider Côte des Blancs.
Vitryat.grape_share_note: Share of the planted area of the zone. Union des Maisons de Champagne (UMC), aire géographique tables; the year is not given.

Montgueux.atlas_note: A single chalk hill just west of Troyes in the Aube, mostly Chardonnay. The houses' union counts it in a wider Côte des Blancs, far to the north.
Montgueux.grape_share_note: Share of the planted area of the zone. Union des Maisons de Champagne (UMC), aire géographique tables; the year is not given.

Côte des Bar.atlas_note: The south of the appellation, in the Aube, with two communes in the Haute-Marne. Pinot Noir covers more than four fifths of the vines, on Kimmeridgian marl. It splits into the Bar-sur-Aubois and the Barséquanais, which includes Les Riceys.
Côte des Bar.grape_share_note: Share of the planted area of the zone. Union des Maisons de Champagne (UMC), aire géographique tables; the year is not given.
